findings.title: include_website_name is never used as the serializer predicate
findings.body: ActiveModel Serializers only honors include hooks named include_<attr>?. This method is defined as include_website_name (no question mark), so it is dead code. website_name is therefore always emitted, including when website is blank or URI parsing fails and the method returns nil. The intended omission never happens.

findings.title: website_name bypasses the TL0 anonymous field restriction
findings.body: website is listed in untrusted_attributes, so anonymous viewers of a trust-level-0 user do not receive the website. website_name is a new public attribute and is not included in that list, and nothing else checks scope.restrict_user_fields?. The profile template now renders model.website_name, so the host and path that used to stay hidden are sent to anonymous clients. Previously the client derived the label from model.website, which was absent in that case.

findings.title: Same-site check treats any hostname suffix as the forum domain
findings.body: The else branch treats the site as the same domain whenever Discourse.current_hostname ends with '.' plus the website host. That is true for any suffix, not only a parent domain: a forum at forum.example.com will treat a website host of com (or example.com.evil is not the issue, but com and other intermediate suffixes are) as internal and append the path. A user website of http://com/user is therefore labeled com/user instead of com. The equal-label sibling check above has the same over-match for unrelated hosts that only share a tail (evil.example.com vs forum.example.com).
